$comment: Performance budgets, measured in CI on every push. See scripts/perf-budget.mjs.
These are ceilings, not targets. A number here should be comfortably above
today's measurement and comfortably below the point at which a phone on a
hotel wifi starts to suffer — a budget set to the current value flags every
commit and gets raised reflexively until it means nothing.
Raising one is a deliberate act with a reason attached, in the same commit
as whatever needed the room. That is the entire mechanism: not that the
numbers are perfect, but that growing past them has to be noticed.

bundles.name: app JavaScript (gzipped)
bundles.why: The one number a phone on a bad connection actually feels. Today ~98KB; 140KB is roughly a second of 3G and the point at which the shell stops feeling instant. Demo Mode is excluded and capped below: no page load can fetch it, only choosing a scenario can.

bundles.name: app CSS (gzipped)
bundles.why: Render-blocking, so it is worse per byte than the JavaScript. Today ~7.7KB.

bundles.name: HTML shell
bundles.why: The document itself. Today ~1.6KB; growth here usually means something got inlined that should not have been.

bundles.name: everything the browser must fetch to render (gzipped)
bundles.why: The total, so splitting one large file into three does not quietly pass three budgets. Demo Mode is the one thing left out, because it is genuinely not on the render path — and it has a ceiling of its own directly below, so the exclusion buys nobody any headroom.

bundles.name: Demo Mode, fetched only when a scenario is opened (gzipped)
bundles.why: Scenario fixtures and the engines that read them. Nothing on a page load can reach these — every path to them is a dynamic import behind Settings or an explicit ?demo= — so they are budgeted apart from the shell rather than against it. Today ~69KB. It has a ceiling all the same: fixtures are the easiest thing in this repository to add carelessly, and the day this fails is the day they should start being loaded per scenario rather than per family.

$flowComment: Interaction budgets, enforced by e2e/performance.spec.ts against a real
WebKit iPhone viewport. Wall-clock in CI is noisy — a shared runner can be
three times slower than a laptop — so these are deliberately generous and
exist to catch a flow going from milliseconds to seconds, not to police
